summary.headline: Page Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 14.1% to INR12,526 million on 10.8% volume growth; FY26 EBITDA margin 22%, guided to 19-21% for FY27.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 14.1% YoY to INR12,526 million, with volume up 10.8% to 54.5 million pieces and PAT up 9% to INR1,787 million. Management attributed the pickup to better consumer sentiment, a correction in distributor inventory that aligned secondary and primary sales, and product upgrades, with March the strongest month. EBITDA margin was 20.8% in the quarter and 22% for FY26, but management guided to a 19-21% range for FY27 citing marketing normalising to 5% of sales, input cost inflation and technology investments. Price increases were small: a 2% weighted average taken in January on product enhancements, with a further price increase planned in Q1 FY27 to cover input costs.

segments.name: Channel: E-commerce / D2C
segments.commentary: E-commerce is about 15% of top line, up roughly 2 percentage points vs last year; Jockey is stated to be number one in men's and women's innerwear across major platforms. Management reads consumer sentiment from EBO jockey.in, where Q4 showed a decent uplift versus the first three quarters.

segments.name: Category: Outerwear and athleisure
segments.commentary: Athleisure is reviving after distributor inventory correction; outerwear and value-added premium products are supporting premiumisation. Management did not give category-level growth numbers.

segments.name: Network
segments.commentary: About 116,600+ multi-brand outlets, 1,615 exclusive brand stores and 893 large-format stores. One large-format store was exited over commercial negotiations, reducing LFS count.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided to 19-21%, versus 22% in FY26; management said it is not expected to be as elevated as last year.
Marketing spend to rise from a little over 4% of sales in FY26 to close to 5% in FY27.
Management targets double-digit volume growth into FY27 and a better volume-value performance than FY26 (value-volume gap of about 4 points in Q4).
A further price increase is expected in Q1 FY27 to cover input cost inflation; management has not decided how much will be passed on to consumers.
Odisha subsidies expected at about INR40-50 crore in FY27; none realised in FY26. Management cautioned that the amount will vary, particularly wage subsidy tied to hiring.
New distribution management system rollout planned over the next year.
capex_capacity: Odisha and K.R. Pet plants are still on the learning curve at suboptimal efficiency; management sees margin upside once they mature.
New technology investments described as unprecedented for Page; these add to costs in FY27.
Inventory built up deliberately in Q4 as a hedge against raw material inflation and for the seasonally heavy Q1.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand improved across categories and channels; March was strong, with January and February also ahead of the first three quarters. Management attributed this to better tertiary sell-out and tighter primary-secondary alignment after distributor inventory correction.

Price increase: 2% weighted average taken from mid-January production, flowing into revenue only from mid-March under FIFO; management said the Q4 price contribution was minimal. Management said the January increase was for product enhancements, not inflation.
Premiumisation (mix shift toward higher-priced products) is the main driver of the roughly 4-point gap between volume and value growth, not price.
Competitive intensity is lower than 1-1.5 years ago in men's and women's, as several D2C brands exited or shrank offline distribution and cut discounting and marketing spend.
Input costs: fresh purchases are seeing elevated inflation, particularly cotton; management declined to quantify the current rate, calling the situation dynamic.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp volume acceleration to double digits, and what initiatives contributed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited better consumer demand in Q4 and recovery in athleisure after distributor inventory correction. Primary and secondary sales are now closely aligned, and March was strong. Management said upstocking was not encouraged and festive timing played little role.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 19-21% EBITDA margin range still hold after input cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management reiterated 19-21% for FY27, citing marketing at 5%, gross margin levels and salary costs as the basis. FY26 margin was higher because marketing was below 5% and gross margin held up.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 margin 22% and why should it moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 benefited from marketing below 5% of sales and sustained gross margin. Normal marketing at 5% plus input inflation will pressure EBITDA, though not to the 22% level.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 2% price increase cover raw material inflation, and will there be more price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: The January 2% increase was for product enhancements, not inflation. A Q1 FY27 price increase is planned to cover input costs, with the pass-through share still undecided. Management said it would absorb costs if volumes were at risk.

qa_highlights.question: Will price hikes hurt volume elasticity in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to price only to the extent volumes are unaffected and would rather absorb cost temporarily in margin than cut volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of market share in economic segment and the new product pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product upgrades launched in Q3 and Q4 were well received. Groove 3 is being extended to about 500 EBOs, select MBOs and e-commerce, and the men's Bonded collection outdoor campaign launched around 20 May.

qa_highlights.question: Are digital-first brands taking share, and is distribution friction behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce has grown for 3-4 years and Jockey ranks number one on major platforms in core categories. Auto replenishment has settled in for about 2.5 years, and a new distribution management system is being rolled out over the next year.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation, particularly cotton and fresh purchases; management has not quantified current inflation.
Margin trajectory: FY27 guided at 19-21% vs 22% in FY26, with marketing rising to about 5% and technology costs.
Price elasticity of the planned Q1 FY27 price increase on double-digit volume growth.
Quarterly sales normalisation (Q1 at 25%, Q4 at 24% of annual sales versus older 28% and 20% patterns) makes Q4 growth harder to read as run-rate.
Odisha subsidy amounts are variable and depend on hiring; the INR40-50 crore estimate is not a recurring figure.
Higher inventory days (73 vs 64 at start of year) and a new distribution system rollout.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and volume momentum, with management stating the distributor inventory correction is over. Cautious on margins: it guided lower to 19-21% and kept pricing and input cost decisions open, which it framed as a choice between absorbing and passing on costs.
key_quotes: So it's a combination of two things. We are seeing -- we've witnessed better tertiary performance at the consumer level in quarter 4.
But our range, we believe, will be between 19% and 21%, and that's what we'll be targeting for the coming year as well.
Our intent in the year going forward is a volume growth intent.
Premiumization is not a result of a price increase.

adds.what: Odisha and K.R. Pet plants ramping on learning curve at suboptimal efficiency (no new capacity quantified)

growth.why: Management targets double-digit volume growth into FY27 with a better volume-value gap than FY26, backed by demand recovery after distributor destocking, lower competitive intensity and premiumisation, but no specific capacity, order or contract numbers were given; FY27 EBITDA margin guided to 19-21% versus 22% in FY26.
